stanza: Grass grows in the icebox
The year ends in the next room
It is autumn and my camouflage is dying
Go find a jukebox
And see what a quarter will do
I don't wanna talk
I just wanna go back to blue
Feeds me when I'm hungry
And quenches my thirst
Loves me when I'm lonely
And thinks of me first
Suffering jukebox
Such a sad machine
You're all filled up with what other people mean
And they never seem to turn you up loud
Got a lot of chatterboxes in this crowd
Suffering jukebox
In a happy town

matchbox.line: We live in a house the size of a matchbox
stanza: My name is secluded
We live in a house the size of a matchbox
Roaches live with us wall to wall
You've killed all our leaders
I don't even have to do nothing to you
You'll cause your own country to fall

padlocks.line: Nightsticks and water cannons, tear gas, padlocks
stanza: Well, the rifleman's stalking the sick and the lame
Preacherman seeks the same, who'll get there first is uncertain
Nightsticks and water cannons, tear gas, padlocks
Molotov cocktails and rocks behind every curtain
False-hearted judges dying in the webs that they spin
Only a matter of time till night comes stepping in

paradox.line: The clock ticks and tocks I think time is a paradox
paradox.linePrev: I want to get under your skin like ticks
paradox.lineNext: I have too many thoughts to talk

sidewalks.line: I used to march down the windy, windy sidewalks
stanza: I used to march down the windy, windy sidewalks
Slapping my leg with a riding crop
Thinking it made me come off so tough
I didn't smile, because a smile always seemed rehearsed
I wasn't afraid of the bullies, and that just made the bullies worse
On the Sunday morning sidewalks
Wishing, Lord, that I was stoned
Cause there's something in a Sunday
That makes a body feel alone
And there's nothin' short of dyin'
Half as lonesome as the sound
On the sleepin' city sidewalks
Sunday mornin' comin' down

sidewalks.line: Where the spew stains on the sidewalks
stanza: And the bowels of his city
Have been locked into a safe
Where the spew stains on the sidewalks
Are defenders of his faith
